speaker: Speaker 1
words: They put it down. Derrick? Huh? Derrick? Oh, yeah. It was Derrick. But they used a certain name for that thing. And I don't know what it is, but I've just forgotten right now. And thought of it for years. And so, but you know, that took them about two months to think that well. I thought they never was going to get it. And so, I went to the, the doctor and they said, you know, Well, Larry. Well, thank you for doing this. 15 cents for dinner, the children were playing around there. He said, well, Mr. Hager had not completely lost it. I said, what's that? And he said, we struck the water. And he said, we cannot lower it. He said, it just seems like it's on a stream and it can't be lowered. He said, we've been out there for over four hours trying to lower that thing. So he said, I guess we'll just have to cap a couple of holes now. And Dan, he said, we'll have to go and get a windmill. And when Dan come in, the little monster boy said, go ahead. He said, we'll take a tank to go and get the windmill.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You talked about the children playing around. Huh? I said, you talked about the children playing around when he came in. How did you pack your water before you had the well?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: We packed it from black rock in the barrel and had a sifter dug and poured it in there. And of course, that sifter was covered over perfectly tight. And it had a, it was so tight that they put a little pump in so you could pump it out, you know. And then I had to carry it from the sifter into the house.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And how many years did you do that before you got to the well?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I suppose, there was about a year. I don't know, six or eight months to dig in that well. Maybe there wasn't as long as I thought there was. I think there were, ever been that long. And mercy in heaven, when they got that windmill on there and got it set up, and Dan then had a tank there. The whole water was a horror. And they filled that up and they filled everything up. And it's cold. That water was just blue and crystal clear. And it was cold as ice.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Just like ice was. And did you ever have to do anything about water again? Never.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Not, I think that well is still going. I don't know for sure. It was when we rented it anyway. And sold it. Yeah. So I guess it is yet, but I don't know for sure. That's a bad thing.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You were telling me the other day about this little house that you built.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah, that was just a homestead house, we called it. It was just 20 by, 18 by 28 or something like that on the floor. And it was, Dan put a floor up there when he built it. So that made a place up there where you could have a bed. And there was a window in it. And that's about all.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Well, I've seen pictures of the house in the big bin. It was a big white house. Now, did you build that?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Was that one?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I thought so.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I think I got a picture of our house around from the big bin here someplace.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: But was that the same house as your original house?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, it could have been part of it. After we, after 513, I think we were there a year or two, and Dad's father, you know, Dad's father and mother were divorced, I suppose. Yeah. Yeah. Well, they were. And he lived in Ritzfield. But when he found out Dan was over there on the farm, that he wanted to come over there. And so there was 160 acres that he could file on. And he wanted to file on that. So Dad took him and let him file on. And that's where we built that house, was on that 160 acres of he had served. He didn't have any money to spend at all. And so we had him. And when, oh, I guess we lived in that two years. Oh, you see, I told you Dan had this 640 acres. Well, we built a house over there too. You know, so we, there was some of Dan's cousins came off from Iowa. And when they come and saw the kind of house we were living in, you know, it was just a house with a roof one story high, you know. And boardroom. And they just had a door, it was a door window. And when they saw it, boy, when they come on the inside, it just looked different. Well, it was like a house.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Well, now this is not the original Homestead house.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, yeah, that's that Homestead house.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Oh, it was. Yeah. Is this the one that was painted blue?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: In the first place. Well, anyway, so Black, our neighbors, this is Black. She's one of the first women I got. Our Black wife, you know, I tell them you come down here. Well, we lived there. We were neighbors for years and years.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: In the Big Bend country?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, the Big Bend. And they come out, they didn't have nothing. They bought land and farmed and they built a house and built a barn. And just like anybody, when they progress, you know, so they can. Well, so they had a Homestead house. It was quite a good house. And Dan bought it. They built this big house. Then Dan bought that Homestead house. See, they had three children and it was a pretty big house. It had a front room, two bedrooms, and a kitchen. No dining room. Eight in the kitchen. And there was a porch on the porch. And Dan took them two houses together and they made quite a house. And they painted them white. I bet that's what you said.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I'm sure that's what I said.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I think I've got the picture of that around here somewhere.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: With a great big team of horses sitting in the front or standing in front of it.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, anyway, then Dan was able to live. You know, he had it all sealed up in paper, then wallpaper put on it, and it looked like a household, you know. Paintings and woodwork put on it.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: A big screened-in porch? Yeah. That was the one I was...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: And so that's where you built that house.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You were talking about she had children. Huh? You were talking about Mrs. Black's children.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, she had three.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And your children and stuff. What medical services were available when your children were born? What? What medical services were available?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I'll tell you. There was a Wilson Creek and...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: That town over there. Oh, that's quite a little town. It's still down there. I'll think of it pretty soon, maybe. And there was a doctor there. There was a doctor at Wilson Creek, too. And then finally they had one of Laura's at the front.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: But did you have your children at home? Huh? Did you have your children at home? Yes.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: All the children were at home. There was a whole camp of folks, possibly as far as I know.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: From the front?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: From down there.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: From down there.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: And the children all lived in every town. As the doctor of course.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Now, what factors affected the number of children you had? Huh? How did you decide upon the number of children you had?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I just had them and then finally I took Ben's case. And didn't get the family anymore.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And that was that, huh?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: That was that.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: If you were to marry again, would you have the same number of children?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: If I were to marry who?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I said if you were to marry again, would you have the same number of children?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I suppose so. I always had the children. I had a hard time having them, being born, you know. But after I was born and everything was fine, I just, in a week I kept doing the work just like ever.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Always. Never bothered you that much? And where was, uh, where was your family when your children were born? Were they right there or...?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, you mean it was at home? Yeah. Yes. I remember when, uh, out here in the ranch, you know, that was in dawn. When dawn was born, I had in, uh...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: What was the name of that couple that worked there?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I forgot his name. They were falling. And, uh, they were upstairs. But I never yelled or made any big noise like that. And Dr. Burns was the doctor.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And Grandpa was there? Huh? And Grandpa was there?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Sure. But that is, you know, incredible.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Well, I thought maybe at the time, it was born.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Oh, yeah. It was at nine. And so they came in the next morning, but when, uh... I'll bet you know that boy. If I could just think of his name, but I can't think of his right now. He, he dressed, come downstairs and went on out taking care of the horse. One candy come down and said, you've got a new brother. And he, he couldn't believe it. There was dawn.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Ah, did you...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: And you don't know who took care of him?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: No, that's what I...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: It was her fern mother. Oh. She was there.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Did you have a midwife? Huh? Did you ever have a midwife?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, well, no. Never had a... The doctor generally came. And I always had a, a hired girl, but I knew I was too pretty to have a, to have a baby.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: But, uh...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: It was her mother. When I... Damn, I went down and asked her if she was kidding me. What she said, I didn't know she was going to have a baby. And I saw her just not long ago. But she come on out, she stayed all night, all day, and the next day. Then the next day, I had this... I can't think of that girl's name. She came, and she was just staying with somebody down here in town, I think. And they was just about through with her. Then she come up and stayed, stayed with me. So, stayed two or three weeks.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: With Don.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: With Don, right. But I never had no trouble after the baby was born. You know. I never was poor. I never had to be soldiering. Huh? No, that's when they left the big bed.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Yeah. And moved to Spokane. Do you remember what year that was? Well, then you were only retired in Spokane for a few months? Before you came to Genesee? I said, were you in Spokane only a few months? Before you came to Genesee?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: We went up there. It's quite nice out there in Spokane. It was 1110 9th Street. And it's still there. We go by once in a while to see it. It's a... It's quite a nice place. That was 1110 9th Street in Spokane. And that's a... You could see it if you ever went up there and went out there.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And... So...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: We lived there and Kenny was born there. Right there. Now that's just how...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And you said he was about two years old then. Okay. When you come to Genesee. Well...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: He wasn't no two years old.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I thought you did. I just couldn't remember.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Don't you know how Lottie and Mrs. Davies used to quarrel over it? Lottie was a... Lottie Davies, that's Mr. Davies' daughter. And she was a... She was going through school, but... Learning to be a nurse, you know. And she had two or three years. I think she had another year or so. Before she was just supposed to take care of Kenny, you know. And Mrs. Davies, she's an old boss. Couldn't do nothing with her. And I was scared to death that we were going to get in trouble with her. And I told Lottie, I said, Lottie, I said... They grew up in here very long, I said... Let her, if you want to... She's an oldie, yes. I have her Kenny, I have Dr. Mills.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You breastfed your baby?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, I breastfed every one of them. And I had plenty of milk. But... She cooked and ate. And she did everything she could. And feed, you know. And Lottie was just mad at her. First of all, they never thought of her at all. She was like half a dog. So, there I had them to fight with. And I couldn't say nothing. I was afraid of Mrs. Davies. She was...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: She was kind of a show woman, you know.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Had been. She was married to Davies. And her kids were in Solway City. And they were show people too. And so...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: What do you mean by show people?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, they had jobs. They were in the theater business. Showing. They had...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Were they actors? Yeah.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: They had... I think she said she had three. See, I never saw one of them. I saw the picture. Never saw them. And...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: So...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: But she was getting ready to leave, you know. The place was sold. And they was going to... Gold shop in California.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And so...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: She was just buzzing around.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Hurry up. Hurry up.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: So I had to do it. It takes time, dear. I can just hear him. Making that beautiful picture. Oh, that's beautiful. And he had to make great pictures. Get them in.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Pictures of what?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Oh, pictures.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: How... Pictures you hang on the wall? Yeah.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Pictures that great people... In beautiful frames. Well, that's why I... Pictures. For faculty. It's bad. Well, then pictures, one or two. That old big leather chair. Don't you remember that I used to have it? Alice or somebody's got it. Oh, I believe Clarence and Ruby's got it now. I can think so.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: What, a rocking chair? Mm-hmm.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: That old big leather rocking chair. Believe me, it was leather.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Yes, I can remember it now. Do you?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah. Well, I don't know. Does Clarence and Ruby have that?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Well, if they do, they don't have it in their house.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: They don't have it now? Uh-uh. Well, they've got some chair of mine down there in the house.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: That could be. They don't have any rocking chair anyplace.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, Alice and... Let's see, have you heard of the name George? Yes. Well, Alice and George, when they moved to Spokane, they had to park, you know, and they hardly had no furniture in. So Clarence and Ruby gave her that chair, another thing or two, kind of helped fill it up a little bit so they could get a little more money to buy some more stuff. And I've been to Alice when she lived up there in that park. It was a real nice... Have you ever been in it? Oh, yes. Well, that was nice, you know. Well, and the last time I visited her up there, you know, her children got big enough and they got a piano. And she got carpets on the floor. I don't remember, but she had that chair in there anymore and all that. I haven't saw Alice. I saw Alice just for a few minutes. Not Alice, but Alice for just a few minutes. What did we have down here?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Black June.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: The reunion? Uh-huh. And she came here just a few minutes. It was real nice. I thought she looked real nice. Uh-huh. And she was here just a little while, and we did. And then I think then she went home with Lisa or somebody. I never saw her again.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Thinking back, Grandma, through the years, what have you done to support your family?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: What have I done? Yeah.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Don't you know? Yes, I do, but I want to get this down. Other people won't know.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: What did you say? I just don't like any other woman.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You took the meals and took care of your family and this sort of thing? I did.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I helped raise, we always raised the deep garden. I always worked in that. Always had lots of chickens and I always took care of them.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And you milked?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, I never milked.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You never did?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Oh, I had milk. Yeah. But no practice of it. I'm not like Rose Parks. You know Rose Parks milks four cows every morning?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: No. Did you know that?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: And she's as pretty as a picture. She's here the other day. She's just like a big doll. She's got them pretty eyes, just like Joel.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Joel. Yeah.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: That's what makes Joel kind of pretty, is him eyes that he's got. And Mrs. Parks has eyes just like...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: But you used to milk, because I can remember seeing you milk.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Oh, I milked, yes. Well, I never made a practice. You know when Dan had that heart attack and had to go and have that... And we lived down there in the flats. Well, I milked. I think that Danny and I had done the milking. We had six cows. And when it was too expensive when it was out on the farm, I mean, I never milked. The men, quite a lot of the time, you know, we had lots of the men. Francis Fisher, Gene Woodruff, those boys, they had to milk. We had a lot of cows. We sold, I think, about a five-gallon cream every day.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Do you remember about how many cows you did have?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: How many cows we milked? Yeah. Seven or eight, I think. I think we sold a five-gallon can, and they had to keep it. We didn't have no refrigerators. We had to keep it down in that well. But we got it tonight. And in the morning, they milked, put it in there. And the men, Dan had to take it out to that road there, you know. Every morning? Every morning. Worked at this installer. I don't even know what we got for it or not.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You actually sold it, rather than, oh, like you used to sell eggs to the grocery store. For groceries? Well, you never traded cream like that, did you?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I never sold cream to the grocery store.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Did you ever make butter and sell it?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, if I ever made any butter, everybody would ask. Boy, oh, boy. When we first met, oh, that cheap man took it. After we was there about seven or eight, or a year, I don't know how long, he got that little red cow, and she was just full of milk. And it was rich. And I had every butter, that's her butter, butter, butter. If I'd had five cows, I think I could have sold every bit of butter. But I don't make any butter. We ate some butter, too.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: What did you do for cooking and milk and stuff before you got this cow after you were married? A can. Can?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Can milk.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Can milk.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Just had to have it. That's all I had.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Now, at one time, Grandpa made sausage and sold it.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Oh, then you sold that. That was in later years. He used to take calls and be very careful about putting in not very hardly any fat.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Now, this is when you lived in Genesee.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: That's when we lived in Genesee, yeah.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Did you help make this? Huh? Did you help make the sausage?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Dad and another man grounded it.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Where did they do it?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: A big tub full of the sausage. Were two. That two tubs of her. And they had it. He'd take it down to Lewis and said, boy, it would be sold right now. He just liked that. He sold it.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Where did they do this? Huh? Where did they make the sausage?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: On the porch in the fall. And then in the winter, they done it in the basement. And they raised it. Boy, we didn't do it all the time either. You know, it's just when they had the halls that would fit for it. Then, we'd take these fat halls and grind them up like they do now. You know, you go to buy coffee, now they have bars.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I can remember you making great big crocks of milk in the cottage cheese.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, I did lots of cottage cheese.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And how did you do this?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I always had that big, big pan. Big, granite, big pan like this one over there, a lot bigger. And put it in there, put it on the stove. And I had to let it sour first. That's the way I had to do it. And then I'd put it on the stove. And you can't, it's got to get real awful hot but not boil. Because boiled, that ruins it. And then I'd have to stir it, you know. And then it would separate the whey would come up in the cow. Then I'd have to strain it through a strainer. And then put cream and salt in it.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And you used to make vinegar too, didn't you?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, never made vinegar. Made lye, not lye, yeah, I made lye soap. I made bar after bar after bar of soap. I could make soap with just a white knife and pretty as cookie.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And you baked lots of, done lots of baking.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I just wonder how it was. Well, I just take it in, you know, once in a while I'd burn something. And I wonder, because if I saw all that stuff that I'd burn, how much would it be?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Well, I bet it wouldn't be too much because you haven't burned all that much. I don't know. I just wonder.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Never once in a while have I burned something. You have to watch it.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: The years that you cooked for...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: The Thor, he just thought, the years the Thor worked out there. Thor thought he never saw anybody make so much bread in all his life. I think Lupe did make that much bread.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Probably. I think so.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: But he had to see her doing it. He'd go over to her and he'd say, I made bread. When Thor first came out there, he was so hungry. He just, Thor just ate everything. And after he got filled up with energy, he just ate the bread.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: What did you, how did you keep meat? Did you always have access to a locker?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, you know, we never, we butchered a beef in the fall after it got, so it freezed outside. And we'd just leave it hanging out there. And then it got so bad that when Dan butchered, why, we would cut it up in pieces and put it in half-gallon jars and cook it.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Do you remember when you started that about?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, before the refrigerators come. I know Ava Nelson was there one day and she said, Mother, don't you think what you're doing is all right to me? And I said, but next fall it won't be. And a lot of people said, I said, look, declare. They said, how come your mother always has fresh meat? And they said, she can't. And how come you can't? Boys that worked there. Jimmy, we had lots of boys that worked there. I couldn't begin to tell you. And a lot of times they come here now. Every once in a while there's a boy come here. I don't know them. To visit.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Huh? To visit.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah, well, they just come to see how I am. Ask if I remember, but I don't. I can't remember anything. Not even their names. I just can't. Oh, Marcy, we had hundreds of them, you know. Different sides, different themes. Just depends on what we was doing. Making hay, you know, we used to make lots of hay.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I can remember.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: For something that large. And, um, and we always had to board the man. They never brought no lunches. That wasn't the custom. You know. So, that's what we did.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Well, um, did you always have a, a tracking machine of some sort?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Combine. Combine. Why, uh, I want the chicken. All I had to do was send Irene out. Back there she'd come with the chicken. She could get it in no time. Oh, there was times she'd get, she'd reel it all out. Had to get her her own. I get you in a beautiful home, one day.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Um, you were talking once about when you lived down in corrupt Washington that you, when you were first married, that you cooked for, uh, a neighbor.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Eggbert.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And you got one dollar, and Grandpa worked for him and he got three dollars.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Huh. Just reels and links.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: How did you feel about the fact that Grandpa got so much more than you got?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I guess I thought it was all right because he had to drive the header bed. Did you ever see a header bed?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I don't know if I did or not.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Huh. Well, that's what he had to drive was a header bed. And he had to take care of some horses.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Do you feel that he worked harder than you?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, yeah, uh, I'd have an afternoon off, you know. I didn't have to be working all the time.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: But then you had to work in the evenings after supper.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: That's right.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Well, about the same number of hours.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: All they had out there, the Eggbert's, you know, was a big long table. Wasn't much housekeeping there. They just had them old hoons, that old hoon set of howls. Then, that early, you know. They had a big long table, I guess it was. Wasn't as wide as that. It was about four, four foot wide, I think. Four foot board. And it was long.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And, uh. Just a regular harvest table.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah, just for a man to eat on. That's all it was for. And, uh, so.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I had to.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: They had the oil sauce on the table. And all you had to do was boil the oil.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: What advice would you give a young woman that would best prepare her for farm life or life in a small town?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, you said, what advice would I give a young woman for what?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: To best prepare herself for farm life. Or life in a small town.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, first I'd have to know that she likes it. I would never try to persuade somebody to go on to a farm that isn't one. Because there's work there, and it's different. Unless they're rich, they're starving.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: But the work is still there.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, yeah, the work is still there, just the same. But then they can have more conveniences. But we'll say they would just want to go to the wild. Now, she could have a refrigerator. And maybe electric stove. And, uh. I'd tell her she'd have to be, have her mind made up that she wanted to do that. And if she did, she'd never be told that. I don't think. Or the work. And effectively, nowadays, I think, to take a young girl, I'd much rather be doing what, that, out on a farm someplace. Where I had, uh. Where I had a refrigerator and stove. And a house to live in. You know, Laura Lee Qualley lives down there in Mrs. Wilson's house now, you know. Oh, no. Oh, you didn't know her. Well, she and her husband live in the lower part of that house. Well, she goes to, a mosque goes, and she goes to Spokane. And that's all the place they could get jobs.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You mean Lewiston?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah. Spokane. Lewiston. She has to go to Lewiston. She goes to mosques. You think of that. She has to, you know. And I always, I get up at about half past five, quarter of six. And I'll, first thing I do is look out to see if Laura Lee is up. Oh, there's a light there. They somehow pulled the light. Laura Lee's on the roof.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You don't think she'd like that?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: If we can both go to the same place, that's such an expense, that's too hard. Yeah.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: How do you figure that farm life differs from, the life of a farm wife differs from that of a city wife?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I don't think there's any comparison. If you're able to live in the city. Look at Allison, what a nice time she's had. She's got a nice home, all fixed. And it has Joel. And Joel, who, did you know she worked in the bank? Yeah, she worked in the bank.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I didn't know that. What?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: That isn't any criteria. She went down there and went to work in the bank. Mail and pallets come in there with the cigar. And they just sat there and they smoked it all out. And Alice made use of it. And she got so sick. Oh, she got depressed sick. There was no window she could open, you know, or anything. And the next day she was vomiting and she couldn't go to work. What was that? Oh, it was vomiting. But in a couple of days, the next morning the phone rang. We were just eating breakfast. And she said, oh, Daddy, she said, I'm so sick. I want you to come down and get Joel breakfast. So, or Dad said he was just eating his breakfast. Well, she said there's no hurry. Damn it. There she was just, she was going to catch her breath all night.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: She was really rich.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I asked her if she was going back to work anymore. She said yes. But it made me made me wouldn't come into that big cigar.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: What magazines do you take, Graham? Huh? What magazines do you take?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Good housekeeping and I've taken Better Homes and Gardens. And, well, I take the Digest and I take, I, I, I let Better Homes and Gardens go. I can't work in the gardens up there anymore. So I said, it's just a loose case. They went up twice in price. And even the, with housekeeping, I have to pay five or six dollars for that. But I'm looking for, I like the stories in that.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Um, newspaper?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I take the Tennessee News and Send. A little, a little contributor. That's a little contributor something. Forty-eight dollars for a year. Forty-eight dollars.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I know. What TV shows do you like? Huh? What TV shows do you like?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Clark Will. I like all the families for once or twice. But they quarrel all the time and then I don't like them. All, all. You know, I, I can put in there a tale of what they're going to do when they come off the family. But I always like Clark Will. Or say some other, you know, once in a while there's a man comes in that comes off real good and I can hear him. And, uh, so I like that. But all that slapping of women and all that, I don't like. I just don't care for them. I don't know whether women are trying, what is women trying to do? Are they trying to take men's place or what? They, they want equal rights. I don't think they should ask that. I don't think women should try to do men, men's work in the army and stuff like that. Now maybe you do, but I don't think so.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I don't think they strictly want to take jobs away from men.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Oh, I don't want to take away from them, but they want equal rights.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And you feel that...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: There's something that a woman can do, a man can't do. That's for sure.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Such as? Huh? Such as what are you talking about?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, uh, I think when it comes to being a nurse, I think a woman makes a better nurse than a man by far.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: There are men nurses though.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Oh, yes. It has to be. And, uh, and when it comes to lifting and things like that, unless you're awful strong, you'll not last so long, I don't think. Because men are built for that. They've not got the... They haven't got the woman's makeup on the inside to stand that lifting and doing things like that. And if they want to go into the army, I think that's so silly, because they have to menstruate every month. But I don't see how they can hardly get along and do that. And they... Well, some of the women couldn't because they get this pain. I never had no trouble. Do you have trouble?

speaker: Speaker 2
words: How would you compare your life now to 20, 30, 40, 50 years ago?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, knowing what I do now, I think it would be pretty hard to go back and live like, you know, the kerosene lamps, for instance. I had eight lamps out there. Don't you know my old shelf back there? Used to have them, eight lamps. They was clean and filth every two or three days.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: There were a lot of other inconveniences.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Now, that's one thing. The electricity, sure. And then, I haven't no washer and dryer, but I would have if I had a place to put it. But I don't know where I'd ever put it. So maybe I'll get it sometime. Bob, one time, Bob Marger, he promised me when he's doing... But he got to working at that other over in Homer,

speaker: Speaker 2
words: or wherever he worked.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: And he got to going so good that he wouldn't stop that for coming to a little job. I wanted to add on a little place on the porch out there and have it sealed up good and tight and put electricity on it. Then I could put a washer and dryer out there. And then it would be better to have a little protection over that door. When people come, they can take off their over shoes and not have to be worried about stuff. Like I tell them, I tell them, it's snow. And you don't have to worry about snow. Mud, that's different. I wouldn't want to attract the mud now, but snow. That melts. So that moth can wipe it up. But mud, that's different. So, and especially now that I'm older. We, you see, they've always had lamps ever since I was born. I never, we never, oh, we had some candles that were old. And did you make them? No, mother never made them.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I can remember you telling about helping your grandmother dip candles.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: But if he was dipping, I never saw one of my grandmothers. Not one of them. Not even one of them.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Um, thinking back, what were some of the things that, that, uh, you most commonly discussed with your, your husband? Huh? I said thinking back, what were some of the things that you most commonly discussed with your husband?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I want to put wheat to wheat tomorrow.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: About the, the price of wheat, huh?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: And then when they were farming, how much of it was taken into that quarter section over there? Oh, we'll be done by noon tomorrow for that. Then where are you going? Oh, on this other path there. And that's just the way it used to go. But we didn't get to do very good this morning. The combine broke down. That's how it's bad. Yeah. And this isn't safe for us.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Well, is there anything else that you'd like to tell about your... Is there anything else you'd like to tell about your experiences? No, I don't think so. I don't think there's anything to it. Not really.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: But I can think of that.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Did you...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: So that I can keep a better date than I did.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Um, I don't think so. Oh, do you think that you were a partner with Grandpa in the farming business?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Not with lots of big business deals. But if he was ever going to do anything, he and I decided. Or talked about it. And anything large enough to... He was quite a big general. Yeah. So, so. I think that's what makes people enjoy each other.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I remember one time...

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Is that thing still on there? Yep. I think I better not tell you. Oh.

speaker: Speaker 2
